_about: Skill metadata for the 22 CTECS Workplace Readiness Skills. Summaries and concept labels are original paraphrases of the public module pages at https://wrs.ctecs.org/practice/ (reviewed 2026-10-18). Concepts are the assessable ideas each module lists; definitional bullets are recorded in notAssessedDirectly because the platform teaches application, not vocabulary recall.

skills.name: Creativity and Innovation
skills.summary: Brings original, resourceful ideas to work and improves how things are done.

concepts.label: Brainstorming and contributing ideas, strategies and solutions
Developing or improving products, services or processes
Identifying and allocating available resources creatively
Recognizing why originality matters in a workplace setting

skills.name: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving
skills.summary: Uses sound reasoning to analyze a problem, weigh solutions and act on the best one.

concepts.label: Recognizing and analyzing the real problem (including root cause)
Evaluating potential solutions and the resources they need
Using a logical approach to decide
Carrying out and checking an effective course of action

skills.name: Initiative and Self-Direction
skills.summary: Spots needs and gets work done independently, without waiting to be told.

concepts.label: Making proactive, independent decisions within one's role
Identifying workplace needs before they become problems
Completing tasks with minimal direct supervision
Applying a solution once a need is identified

skills.name: Integrity
skills.summary: Follows laws, procedures and policies and is honest, fair and respectful toward people and property.

concepts.label: Complying with local, state and federal requirements (taught only when the scenario states the rule)
Adhering to workplace policies and procedures
Being honest and fair toward others, including accurate reporting
Treating the property and resources of others with respect
Seeing the workplace consequences of acting with or without integrity

skills.name: Work Ethic
skills.summary: Works diligently, can be counted on, and owns the results of decisions and actions.

concepts.label: Persisting to finish a task well
Being reliable about commitments and coverage
Accounting for one's own decisions and actions
Accepting the consequences of one's decisions and actions

skills.name: Conflict Resolution
skills.summary: Works out workable solutions to disagreements caused by personality, culture, work style or performance.

concepts.label: Negotiating diplomatic solutions and compromises
Handling conflicts rooted in different work styles
Raising and responding to performance concerns constructively
Handling conflicts rooted in personality or cultural differences
Deciding when a supervisor needs to be involved

skills.name: Listening and Speaking
skills.summary: Listens closely, asks clarifying questions, and speaks in a way that suits the audience and setting.

concepts.label: Reading and using nonverbal cues
Active listening: clarifying questions and paraphrasing
Public speaking and giving presentations
Fitting message, method and detail to the audience and setting

skills.name: Respect for Diversity
skills.summary: Values individual differences and works well with people of different backgrounds, views and experiences.

concepts.label: Recognizing differences such as age, culture, ability, viewpoint and background
Showing respect for and valuing those differences at work
Noticing and checking one's own assumptions and bias
Collaborating with people whose backgrounds and views differ

skills.name: Customer Service Orientation
skills.summary: Anticipates and meets the needs of customers and coworkers with courteous, knowledgeable service.

concepts.label: Serving both internal customers (coworkers) and external customers
Prioritizing service among competing demands
Anticipating the needs of customers and coworkers
Giving courteous, accurate, helpful service and handling complaints

skills.name: Teamwork
skills.summary: Shares responsibility for group work and respects teammates' ideas and contributions.

concepts.label: Establishing expectations, roles and goals
Contributing to team success by sharing responsibility
Respecting the thoughts and contributions of teammates
Keeping teammates informed so the work stays coordinated

skills.name: Big-Picture Thinking
skills.summary: Understands one's role in the workplace mission and considers social, economic and environmental effects.

concepts.label: Connecting one's own work to the organization's mission
Weighing social, economic and environmental effects of actions
Understanding organizational structure, culture, policies and procedures
Seeing the organization's place in its community, industry and economy

skills.name: Career and Life Management
skills.summary: Plans and manages personal and professional goals involving education, career, money and health.

concepts.label: Education, qualifications and advancement planning
Using benefits and professional resources (unions, associations, assistance programs, insurance, retirement)
Managing stress, self-care and personal finances
Setting specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, time-bound goals

skills.name: Continuous Learning and Adaptability
skills.summary: Accepts feedback, stays open to new methods, and keeps building skills as job demands change.

concepts.label: Choosing learning resources (publications, workshops, networks, trade organizations)
Changing performance based on feedback (being coachable)
Pursuing industry credentials and certifications
Adapting to changing job requirements

notAssessedDirectly: describing the importance of continuous learning

skills.name: Efficiency and Productivity
skills.summary: Plans, prioritizes and adapts work goals to use time and resources well.

concepts.label: Developing a plan of work
Telling high-priority from low-priority tasks
Adapting work goals to the time and resources available
Using people's strengths and respecting their goals
Maintaining equipment so it lasts and works efficiently
Using responsible, sustainable practices

skills.name: Information Literacy
skills.summary: Finds information efficiently, judges how credible and relevant it is, and uses it well.

concepts.label: Locating information efficiently
Judging credibility, authority and whether information is current
Judging whether information fits the task at hand
Using information effectively to complete work tasks

skills.name: Information Security
skills.summary: Practices basic internet and email safety and follows workplace protocols that protect information, devices, networks and facilities.

concepts.label: Protecting information in every format (paper and electronic)
Recognizing cybersecurity risks, threats and vulnerabilities
Using technology and social networks ethically; managing personal information
Following workplace acceptable-use policies
Protecting confidentiality (logins, customer information)
Following workplace security procedures, including reporting incidents

skills.name: Information Technology
skills.summary: Keeps a working knowledge of devices, software, cloud services, file sharing and basic troubleshooting.

concepts.label: Hardware and devices, including peripherals
Choosing and using software and applications
Cloud-based services and file-sharing practices
Responding sensibly to emerging technologies
Troubleshooting protocols and techniques

skills.name: Job-Specific Tools and Technologies
skills.summary: Selects and safely uses the technology, tools and machines a job calls for.

concepts.label: Selecting the right tool, machine or technology for a task
Using tools within training, authorization and manufacturer guidance

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.summary: Applies practical math to complete work tasks and manage personal finances.

concepts.label: Percentages, fractions, averages, measurement, conversions and money transactions
Estimating supplies and completing expense or order calculations
Understanding wages, paycheck deductions, taxes and receipts

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.summary: Meets workplace expectations for schedule, behavior, appearance and communication.

concepts.label: Punctuality, attendance and meeting schedule expectations
Workplace and online etiquette, language and manners
Introducing oneself and representing oneself professionally
Meeting grooming and dress expectations

skills.name: Reading and Writing
skills.summary: Reads and interprets workplace documents and writes clearly, with suitable tone and conventions.

concepts.label: Reading and interpreting workplace documents
Writing messages that convey meaning clearly
Using a professional tone suited to the audience
Grammar, formatting and workplace conventions (such as email signatures)

skills.name: Workplace Safety
skills.summary: Keeps the work environment safe by following safety guidelines and spotting risks to self and others.

concepts.label: Following safety standards and instructor, employer and manufacturer guidelines
Using safety data sheets (SDS) when provided
Identifying and using personal protective equipment
Using universal precautions against bloodborne pathogens
Identifying and reporting risks and hazards
Following emergency protocols such as evacuation routes
